title: Epic Sepsis Model external validation at Michigan Medicine
system_purpose: Predict sepsis onset in hospitalised adults and alert clinicians
decision_impact: Alerts steer clinician attention and the timing of assessment and antibiotics
verified_facts: A peer-reviewed external validation of a proprietary sepsis prediction model deployed at hundreds of hospitals found poor discrimination and calibration in a retrospective cohort of 27697 patients and 38455 hospitalisations between 2018-12-06 and 2019-10-20.
reported_harm: Missed deterioration and alert fatigue reported as measured model behaviour, not as a confirmed patient death count
quantitative_evidence: Area under the curve 0.63 with 95 percent confidence interval 0.62 to 0.64; sepsis occurred in 2552 cases (7 percent); the model did not identify 1709 of 2552 sepsis patients (67 percent) while generating alerts at a score of 6 or higher for 6971 of all 38455 hospitalised patients (18 percent).
limitations: Retrospective single-centre study of an inpatient early-warning model, so it measures model performance and alert burden and does not establish how many patients were actually harmed. The abstract mixes patient-level and hospitalisation-level denominators, so the 7 percent figure is quoted as published rather than recomputed, and none of it transfers directly to app-based triage.

title: Commercial health risk algorithm that predicted cost instead of illness
system_purpose: Rank patients by predicted need to enrol them in extra care management
decision_impact: The score decided who was referred into additional care programmes
affected_groups: Black patients;patients with low prior healthcare spending;care managers
verified_facts: A peer-reviewed study of a widely used commercial algorithm found that at an equal risk score Black patients had more uncontrolled illness than White patients, because the algorithm was trained to predict healthcare cost as a proxy for health need.
reported_harm: Discriminatory allocation of extra care that reduced access for patients whose past care spending was lower
quantitative_evidence: Correcting the target variable would raise the share of Black patients referred for extra help from 17.7 percent to 46.5 percent; the authors state that algorithms of this type affect millions of patients.
limitations: One commercial algorithm in the United States health system; the study identifies the proxy-target mechanism but does not audit our vendor, and United States cost and access patterns are not the Vietnamese ones.

title: NEDA Tessa wellbeing chatbot disabled after giving weight-loss advice
system_purpose: Offer an automated eating-disorder prevention and information resource
decision_impact: The chatbot answered help-seeking users directly with no clinician in the loop
affected_groups: people with eating disorders;help-seeking users;helpline volunteers
verified_facts: Press reporting records that a user with an eating-disorder history received weight-loss guidance from the Tessa chatbot, that the sponsoring association disabled the chatbot on 2023-05-30 within about a day of receiving screenshots, and that the association states the vendor enabled generated answers beyond the original rule-based design without its awareness or approval.
reported_harm: Harmful advice to a vulnerable user, reported through the affected user and the sponsoring organisation rather than through a regulator
quantitative_evidence: No affected-user count is published; the reporting documents one user conversation, a specific calorie and deficit recommendation, and a takedown within roughly 24 hours of the screenshots being shared.
limitations: Journalistic account plus organisational statements with no independent technical audit and no regulator finding; the vendor-change claim comes from the sponsoring organisation, and the scale of exposure is unknown.
